claims.text: Short-range chemical ordering differs among the quinary alloy and its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Differences in short-range chemical ordering produce differences in local lattice distortion.
Variations in short-range order and local lattice distortion explain the alloys' differing mechanical properties.
The Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni quinary alloy has enhanced mechanical properties relative to its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Identical thermomechanical treatments can produce comparable single-phase FCC states in the alloys being compared.
Applying the same thermomechanical processing ensures comparable microstructures across the samples.
The greater chemical complexity of the quinary alloy promotes stronger short-range chemical order than in the quaternary and ternary alloys.
The greater chemical complexity of the quinary alloy promotes more pronounced local lattice distortions.
Short-range chemical order and local lattice distortions obstruct dislocation motion.
Short-range chemical order and local lattice distortions facilitate the operation of multiple slip systems.
The proposed changes in dislocation motion and slip behavior improve yield strength.
The proposed changes in dislocation motion and slip behavior improve ductility.
The quinary alloy will have higher yield strength than the quaternary and ternary alloys under the stated conditions.
The quinary alloy will have greater elongation to failure than the quaternary and ternary alloys under the stated conditions.
The hypothesis is restricted to single-phase FCC alloys subjected to identical thermomechanical processing and quasi-static room-temperature deformation.
The magnitude of the proposed strength and ductility changes may depend on which elements are removed from the quinary alloy.
